spec.title: Splitting a large working tree into atomic commits

p.a-long-session-leaves-the-tree-looking-l: A long prototyping session often leaves the working tree looking like a weather map: changes everywhere, some connected, some not.

p.this-document-is-the-splitting-procedure: This document is the procedure for turning that mess into a sequence of atomic commits without losing or reordering work.

p.THE-TREE-MUST-BUILD-AND-IDEALLY-PASS-TES: Before starting, the working tree must build and (ideally) pass tests.

p.STABILISE-TO-GREEN-BEFORE-SPLITTING-A-BR: If the tree is broken end to end, do not try to split yet — stabilise to a green state first, on a single WIP commit if necessary, then split from the green state.

p.a-broken-starting-point-means-a-moving-t: A broken intermediate during a split is inevitable sometimes, but a broken *starting* point means the split is working with a moving target.

inventory.title: Step 1 — inventory
inventory.fence: git status git diff --stat HEAD git diff HEAD

p.READ-THE-OUTPUT-END-TO-END: Read the output end to end.

p.NAME-EVERY-CHANGED-CHUNK-BY-INTENT-NOT-B: The goal is to name every changed chunk by **intent**, not by file.

p.produce-a-list-lead: Produce a list in a scratch document (or a chat message to the agent):

inventory.fence: - Added retry helper in retry.rs - Used retry helper in http_client.rs - Added test for retry helper - Renamed `conn` to `connection` in connection.rs - Fixed typo in README - Reformatted unrelated imports in lib.rs

p.NOT-NECESSARILY-SIX-COMMITS: Not necessarily six commits — some will collapse together in the next step.

p.collapse-items-that-express-the-same-ide: Collapse items that express the same idea into one commit:

facts.GROUP-EXAMPLE-RETRY-HELPER: "Added retry helper" + "Used retry helper" + "Added test for retry helper" → one commit: `feat(core): retry helper for transient failures`. These three changes are one idea.
facts.GROUP-EXAMPLE-RENAME: "Renamed `conn` to `connection`" → one commit: `refactor(core): rename conn to connection`. Mechanical rename, one concern.
facts.GROUP-EXAMPLE-TYPO-FIX: "Fixed typo in README" → one commit: `docs: fix typo in README`. Trivially one concern.
facts.GROUP-EXAMPLE-REFORMATTED-IMPORTS: "Reformatted unrelated imports" → one commit: `style(core): reformat imports`. Trivially one concern, but see the note below.

p.six-items-collapsed-to-four-commits: Six items collapsed to four commits.

p.reformatted-imports-are-often-an-auto-fo: "Reformatted unrelated imports" is often the footprint of an auto-format-on-save firing during a different task.

p.CONSIDER-REVERTING-AN-UNINTENTIONAL-REFO: If the reformat was not intentional, consider reverting it rather than shipping a `style` commit for it — tidy is not the same as intentional.

p.AN-INTENTIONAL-PASS-IS-A-STYLE-COMMIT-A-: An intentional formatting pass is a style commit; a stray one is cruft.

apply.title: Step 3 — apply

p.USE-GIT-ADD-P-TO-STAGE-EXACTLY-THE-HUNKS: For each planned commit, use `git add -p` (patch mode) to stage exactly the hunks that belong to it.

p.THEN-COMMIT-WITH-THE-APPROPRIATE-CONVENT: Then commit with the appropriate Conventional Commits message (the format is the `git-conventional-commits` flow: `spec://org.vibevm.world/git-conventional-commits/flows/conventional-commits/conventional-commits#root`).

apply.fence:
git add -p # stage retry-feature hunks git commit # message: feat(core): retry helper ...
git add -p # stage rename hunks git commit # message: refactor(core): rename conn ...
git add README.md git commit # message: docs: fix typo in README
git add -p # stage formatting hunks (or skip if accidental) git commit # message: style(core): reformat imports

p.RUN-GIT-STATUS-AFTER-EACH-COMMIT: After each commit run `git status` to verify the remaining tree contains only what has not yet been split — no stray staging, no hidden files dragged in by a wildcard.

p.AVOID-GIT-ADD-ALL-WHILE-SPLITTING: Avoid `git add -A` and `git add .` while splitting.

p.THEY-STAGE-EVERYTHING-AND-DEFEAT-THE-PAT: They stage *everything*, which defeats the patch-mode intent and may pull in files you did not plan to commit (scratch files, credentials, large binary outputs).

p.USE-EXPLICIT-FILE-NAMES-OR-GIT-ADD-P: Use explicit file names or `git add -p`.

verify.title: Step 4 — verify build between commits

p.EACH-INTERMEDIATE-COMMIT-SHOULD-LEAVE-TH: Whenever feasible, each intermediate commit should leave the tree buildable.

p.run-the-build-after-each-commit-lead: Run the build (and ideally tests) after each commit, not only at the end:

verify.fence: cargo build # or the local equivalent cargo test # where fast enough to keep in the loop

p.BROKEN-INTERMEDIATES-ARE-A-BISECT-LIABIL: A split that produces two compilable commits plus two broken intermediate commits is a bisect liability — `git bisect` will hit the broken intermediates and mis-attribute failures.

p.SQUASH-THE-INTERMEDIATES-WHEN-GREENNESS-: If strict between-commit greenness is impractical (for example, a rename that must touch six files atomically and cannot be usefully decomposed further), squash the intermediates so at least the boundary is clean.

p.EACH-SUBJECT-SHOULD-MAKE-SENSE-IN-ISOLAT: Each should make sense in isolation.

p.STOP-ON-AN-UNINFORMATIVE-SUBJECT-LINE: If you see `chore: more stuff`, `wip`, or `fix: address review` in the list, stop — the split is incomplete or the message is uninformative.

delegate.title: Delegating to the agent

p.the-agent-is-better-at-this-than-most-hu: This is a highly mechanical task and the agent is genuinely better at it than most humans under time pressure. A working prompt:

delegate.fence:
I have a dirty working tree. Before committing: 1. Run `git status` and `git diff HEAD`. 2. Name every change by intent (not by file). 3. Group intents into atomic commits. 4. Show me the proposed split as: commit number, subject line, list of files / hunks it will stage. 5. Do NOT run any git commands after the proposal until I approve.
On approval: - Execute the split one commit at a time. - Run `cargo build` (or the local equivalent) between commits. - Stop and surface any build failure before continuing. - Do NOT push. That is a separate, explicit step.

p.THE-HUMAN-VERIFIES-THE-SPLIT-PLAN: The human verifies the **split plan**, not each individual `git commit` invocation.

p.that-is-where-the-division-of-labour-pay: That is where the division of labour actually pays off.

facts.PREPUSH-SKIM-EACH-DIFF: Skim each diff (`git show <sha>`). Subject should match diff.
facts.PREPUSH-CHECK-FOR-SECRETS-AND-STRAYS: Check for secrets, large binaries, or scratch files that slipped in.

p.A-MISTAKE-AFTER-THE-PUSH-MEANS-A-NEW-COM: Fixing a mistake after the push means a new `fix`/`revert` commit, not a force-push.

facts.SUM-STABILISE-THEN-SPLIT: Stabilise to green first; split second.
facts.SUM-INVENTORY-AND-GROUP-BY-INTENT: Inventory by intent, not by file. Group by intent.
facts.SUM-STAGE-HUNKS-WITH-GIT-ADD-P: Use `git add -p` to stage hunks per commit. Avoid `git add -A`.
facts.SUM-DELEGATE-AND-VERIFY-THE-PLAN: Delegate the mechanical split to the agent; verify the plan, not the typing.
facts.SUM-PRE-PUSH-REVIEW-IS-SEPARATE: Pre-push review is a separate, deliberate step.
